options.text: The plan costs this much more: {w2|money0}.
options.why: This subtracts one payment from the price.
options.mis: One payment shows the difference.

options.text: The plan costs this much more: {w3|money0}.
options.why: That is one monthly payment.
options.mis: The monthly payment is the cost.

configs.lesson: Extra cost of a plan = (number of payments × payment) − cash price.

facts: You want to save {G|money0} for a certification course. You already have {have|money0} and can save {s|money0} a month.
prompt: How many months until you reach the goal?

options.why: Subtract what you have, divide by the monthly savings, and round up to whole months.
This ignores the money you already have.
options.mis: Start from zero every time.

options.why: Rounding down leaves you short of the goal.
options.mis: Round to the nearest month.

options.why: Savings arrive in whole months, so round up.
options.mis: Part of a month counts as a month of savings.

configs.lesson: Months needed = ceil((goal − current savings) ÷ monthly savings).

facts: Your order totals {T|money0}. Shipping is {f|money0}, or free on orders of {F|money0} or more.
You also need a {x|money0} item next week.
prompt: What is the cheapest choice overall?

options.text: Add the item now and get free shipping, for {add|money0}
options.why: {T|money0} + {x|money0} reaches the free-shipping level, so you pay {add|money0} for both items.

options.text: Pay shipping now, for {nowpay|money0}, and order the item next week
options.why: That costs {nowpay|money0} now and more shipping later; adding the item now avoids both fees.
options.mis: Ordering only what you need today is always cheapest.

options.text: Add extra items you do not need to be safe
options.why: Buying items you do not need wastes money.
options.mis: More items always mean more savings.

options.text: Pay shipping now and decide about the item later
options.why: This pays a shipping fee you can avoid with an item you already need.
options.mis: Deciding later saves money.

configs.lesson: Count the costs you can avoid, not just today's total.

facts: An item costs the store {C|money0}. It is marked up {m|int} percent, then put on sale for {d|int} percent off the marked price.
prompt: What is the sale price?

options.why: Apply the markup to the cost, then take the discount off the marked price.
This nets the percents, but the discount is taken from the higher marked price.
options.mis: Percent changes can be combined by subtracting.

options.why: This forgets the sale.
options.mis: The marked price is the sale price.

options.why: This takes the discount off the cost and forgets the markup.
options.mis: Discounts apply to the store's cost.

configs.lesson: Apply percent changes one after another, each to the current price.

facts: A part must be {S|int} millimeters long, plus or minus {tol|dec1} millimeters.
You measure four parts: {m1|dec1}, {m2|dec1}, {m3|dec1} and {m4|dec1} millimeters.
prompt: Which part is out of spec?

options.why: {m1|dec1} is within {tol|dec1} of {S|int}.
options.mis: Any difference from the target is a defect.

options.why: {m2|dec1} is within {tol|dec1} of {S|int}.
options.mis: Any difference from the target is a defect.

options.why: {m3|dec1} is within {tol|dec1} of {S|int}.
options.mis: Any difference from the target is a defect.

options.why: {m4|dec1} differs from {S|int} by more than {tol|dec1}.

configs.lesson: A measurement is in spec if it is within the tolerance of the target.

facts: You use about {u|int} {supply.plural} a day. A new order takes {L|int} days to arrive, and policy is to keep {s|int} extra as safety stock.
prompt: At what stock level should you reorder?

options.why: Reorder when stock covers the days until delivery plus the safety stock.
This forgets the safety stock.
options.mis: Safety stock is optional.

options.why: This adds the numbers instead of multiplying daily use by days.
options.mis: All the numbers get added.

options.why: This multiplies the safety stock by daily use.
options.mis: Everything gets multiplied by daily use.

configs.lesson: Reorder point = daily use × lead time + safety stock.

facts: A job pays {r|money0} an hour for {h|int} hours a week. Commuting costs {c|money0} a day for {d|int} days a week.
prompt: What does the job pay per hour after commuting costs?

options.why: Subtract the week's commuting cost from the week's pay, then divide by the hours.
This ignores the commuting cost.
options.mis: Costs of getting to work do not matter.

options.why: This subtracts a full day's commute from each hour.
options.mis: Daily costs apply to every hour.

options.why: This subtracts the whole week's commute from each hour.
options.mis: Weekly costs come out of each hour.

configs.lesson: Net hourly pay = (weekly pay − weekly work costs) ÷ weekly hours.

facts: A school fundraiser costs {F|money0} to set up. Each item sells for {p|money0} and costs {v|money0} to make.
prompt: How many items must be sold to cover the setup cost?

options.why: Each sale earns the price minus the cost to make it; divide the setup cost by that and round up.
This ignores what each item costs to make.
options.mis: The selling price is all profit.

options.why: Rounding down leaves the setup cost not quite covered.
options.mis: Round to the nearest item.

options.why: This divides by the cost to make, not the profit per item.
options.mis: Cost per item decides the break-even.

configs.lesson: Break-even quantity = setup cost ÷ (price − cost per item), rounded up.
